Spinoglio, a nineteenth-century winery, is located north of Montevideo. Vineyards and parkland surround its historic buildings, where modern wine production operates today.

A particularly notable feature is the underground cellar, with massive stone walls and large oak barrels. A visit introduces guests to local winemaking traditions and ends with a tasting of regional wines.

Suchitoto is considered one of El Salvador's most beautiful towns. Its name, in an indigenous language, means "city of birds and flowers." The town lies amid rural landscapes on the shore of Lake Suchitlán and holds National Cultural Heritage status.

Suchitoto's historic appearance survives in its rows of colonial houses and cobblestone streets. The town's flourishing period was linked to the indigo trade.

Today, Suchitoto hosts colorful cultural festivals. The lake, historic architecture and surrounding countryside make it a destination in its own right on a journey through El Salvador.

On the Rio Sucuri, travelers discover the river landscape while drifting gently downstream. The clear water makes it possible to observe fish, plants and the pale riverbed.

A walk along a forest trail comes before the water activity. The visit combines nature watching on land with exploring the river's underwater life.
